CSF in the subarachnoid space passes through these granulations into the venous blood. This completes the one-way loop of CSF, from production in the ventricles to reabsorption into the blood.
notes: The dura mater forms the venous sinuses that receive the CSF, but the granulations that carry the fluid across belong to the arachnoid. Pick the dura if the question asked which layer forms the sinuses.
The pia mater clings to the brain surface and does not form granulations. It would be the answer if the question asked which layer forms the denticulate ligaments.
Ependymal cells line the ventricles and cover the choroid plexus, where CSF is produced, not where it is reabsorbed. Pick them for a question about what lines the ventricles.
Correct. Arachnoid granulations are projections of the arachnoid mater.
questions.answerText: The arachnoid mater

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: The lateral ventricles connect to the third ventricle through which openings?
options: The cerebral aqueduct
The interventricular foramina
The apertures of the fourth ventricle
The central canal
questions.why: Each lateral ventricle opens into the third ventricle through an interventricular foramen, also called a foramen of Monro. This is the first step in CSF flow after the fluid is made in the lateral ventricles. The name describes the location: inter means between, so these foramina lie between ventricles.
notes: The cerebral aqueduct connects the third ventricle to the fourth, one step further along the pathway. Pick it if the question asked how CSF leaves the third ventricle.
Correct. The interventricular foramina link the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle.

The apertures (two lateral and one median) let CSF leave the fourth ventricle for the subarachnoid space, near the end of the ventricular route. Pick them if the question asked how CSF exits the ventricles.
The central canal runs down the spinal cord from the fourth ventricle. It would be the answer for a question about the channel inside the cord.
questions.answerText: The interventricular foramina

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: The third and fourth ventricles are connected by which channel?
options: The central canal
The cerebral aqueduct
An arachnoid granulation
The interventricular foramina
questions.why: The cerebral aqueduct, also called the aqueduct of Sylvius, is a narrow channel running through the midbrain. It carries CSF from the third ventricle in the diencephalon down to the fourth ventricle behind the pons. Because it is so narrow, a blockage here backs CSF up into the third and lateral ventricles and causes hydrocephalus.
notes: The central canal continues from the fourth ventricle down the spinal cord. It would be the answer for a question about the channel below the fourth ventricle.
Correct. The cerebral aqueduct links the third and fourth ventricles.
An arachnoid granulation is where CSF is reabsorbed into the venous blood, at the end of the circulation. Pick it if the question asked where CSF leaves the CNS.
The interventricular foramina connect the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle, one step earlier in the pathway. Pick them if the question asked how CSF reaches the third ventricle.
questions.answerText: The cerebral aqueduct

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which ventricle lies between the brainstem and the cerebellum?
options: The central canal
A lateral ventricle
The third ventricle
The fourth ventricle
questions.why: The fourth ventricle is the CSF space that lies behind the pons and upper medulla and in front of the cerebellum. It receives fluid from the cerebral aqueduct and passes it to the subarachnoid space through its apertures and into the central canal of the cord. It contains choroid plexus like the other ventricles.
notes: The central canal is the CSF channel inside the spinal cord, continuous with the fourth ventricle but not a brain ventricle itself. Pick it for a question about the fluid channel in the cord.
The lateral ventricles lie within the cerebral hemispheres, one on each side. Pick a lateral ventricle if the question asked which ventricle lies in the cerebrum.
The third ventricle lies in the diencephalon, above the brainstem. It would be the answer if the question asked which ventricle is enclosed by the thalami.
Correct. The fourth ventricle lies between the brainstem and cerebellum.
questions.answerText: The fourth ventricle

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A spinal tap, or lumbar puncture, draws cerebrospinal fluid from which space?
options: The subdural space
The subarachnoid space
A dural venous sinus
The epidural space
questions.why: A lumbar puncture withdraws CSF from the subarachnoid space in the lower back, where it widens into the lumbar cistern below the end of the cord. The needle passes the epidural space, then the dura and arachnoid, before CSF appears. Because the cord ends near the L1 to L2 disc, a needle placed lower meets only the floating cauda equina.
notes: The subdural space is only a potential space between the dura and arachnoid and holds no pool of CSF. Pick it if the question asked where a subdural hematoma forms.
Correct. A spinal tap samples CSF from the subarachnoid space.
A dural venous sinus carries venous blood inside the skull, not fluid in the lower back. Pick it if the question asked where CSF drains after reabsorption.
The epidural space holds fat and veins, not CSF, and the needle passes through it on the way in. It would be the answer for where an epidural anesthetic is placed.
questions.answerText: The subarachnoid space

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which meningeal space is normally only a potential space, with a thin film of fluid between its two layers?
options: The epidural space
The subarachnoid space
The subdural space
The lumbar cistern
questions.why: The subdural space lies between the dura mater and the arachnoid mater. Normally these two layers lie against each other with only a thin film of fluid between them, which is why it is called a potential space. It becomes a real space only when something, such as blood from a torn vein, pushes the layers apart.
notes: The epidural space in the vertebral canal is a true space filled with fat and veins. Pick it if the question asked where an epidural injection goes.
The subarachnoid space is a real, open space filled with CSF between the arachnoid and pia. It would be the answer if the question asked which space holds CSF.
Correct. The subdural space is a potential space between the dura and arachnoid.
The lumbar cistern is the enlarged part of the subarachnoid space below the conus medullaris, a large pool of CSF. Pick it if the question asked where a spinal tap draws fluid.
questions.answerText: The subdural space

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: From its Latin name, which meninx is the tough mother on the outside?
options: The falx cerebri
The dura mater
The pia mater
The arachnoid mater
questions.why: Mater means mother, and the meninges are named from tough mother on the outside to tender mother on the inside. Dura means tough, so the dura mater is the tough outer layer. Pia means tender, so the pia mater is the delicate innermost layer, and the arachnoid, named for its spider-web look, lies between them.
notes: The falx cerebri is a fold of the dura that dips into the longitudinal fissure, not a separate meningeal layer. Pick it if the question asked what separates the two cerebral hemispheres.
Correct. Dura mater means tough mother.
Pia means tender, so the pia mater is the tender mother on the inside, clinging to the brain. Pick it if the question asked which name means tender mother.
The arachnoid mater is named for its spider-web appearance, not for toughness. It would be the answer if the question asked which meninx is named after a spider.
questions.answerText: The dura mater

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Hydrocephalus is a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid that enlarges which structures?
options: The subdural spaces
The arachnoid granulations
The dural sinuses
The ventricles
questions.why: In hydrocephalus, CSF builds up because its flow or reabsorption is blocked, so the ventricles fill and enlarge. Because the skull cannot expand in an adult, intracranial pressure rises and the enlarging ventricles press on the brain. Narrow points such as the cerebral aqueduct are common places for a blockage.
notes: The subdural space is a potential space that fills with blood, not CSF, in a subdural hematoma. It would be the answer for a bleed between the dura and arachnoid.
The arachnoid granulations are where CSF is reabsorbed. Poor reabsorption there can cause hydrocephalus, but the structures that swell with fluid are the ventricles.
The dural sinuses carry venous blood and receive reabsorbed CSF, but they are not what enlarges in hydrocephalus. Pick them if the question asked where CSF finally drains.
Correct. Hydrocephalus enlarges the ventricles.
questions.answerText: The ventricles

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: An epidural hematoma is bleeding located between which two structures?
options: The dura mater and the arachnoid mater
The dura mater and the skull
The pia mater and the brain
The arachnoid mater and the pia mater
questions.why: Epi means upon, so an epidural hematoma is a collection of blood on the outside of the dura, between the dura mater and the skull. In the cranium the dura is normally attached to the bone, so the bleeding strips the dura away from the skull as it collects. Each named bleed is defined by which layers it lies between.
notes: Bleeding between the dura and the arachnoid is a subdural hematoma. Pick this pair if the question asked about a subdural bleed.
Correct. An epidural hematoma lies between the dura and the skull.
The pia mater clings directly to the brain with no open space between them. A student who assumes every pair of neighboring layers has a space between them picks this.
The space between the arachnoid and pia is the subarachnoid space, and bleeding there is a subarachnoid hemorrhage, which mixes with the CSF. Pick this pair for a subarachnoid hemorrhage.
questions.answerText: The dura mater and the skull

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Within which structures is cerebrospinal fluid produced?
options: The ventricles
The subarachnoid space
The arachnoid granulations
The dural sinuses
questions.why: CSF is produced by the choroid plexus, networks of capillaries wrapped in ependymal cells, which are found in the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles. The fluid then flows through the ventricles and out into the subarachnoid space. CSF is made inside the ventricles but reabsorbed outside them, at the arachnoid granulations.
notes: Correct. CSF is made in the ventricles by the choroid plexus.
The subarachnoid space holds CSF after it leaves the fourth ventricle, but the fluid is not made there. It would be the answer if the question asked where CSF surrounds the brain.
The arachnoid granulations are the site of reabsorption, the opposite end of the loop from production. Pick them if the question asked where CSF returns to the blood.
The dural sinuses carry venous blood and receive CSF at the end of its circulation. Pick them if the question asked where reabsorbed CSF ends up.
questions.answerText: The ventricles

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: The cranial dura mater has two layers. What are they?
options: An outer periosteal layer and an inner meningeal layer
An outer arachnoid layer and an inner pia layer
An outer meningeal layer and an inner periosteal layer
An outer fibrous layer and an inner synovial layer
questions.why: Around the brain, the dura mater has an outer periosteal layer attached to the inside of the skull and an inner meningeal layer facing the arachnoid. The two are fused except where they part to form the dural venous sinuses. The inner meningeal layer is also the one that folds inward to form the dural reflections, such as the falx cerebri.
notes: Correct. The periosteal layer is outer and the meningeal layer is inner.
The arachnoid and pia are separate meninges, not layers of the dura. Pick them if the question asked which two meninges border the subarachnoid space.
This reverses the layers. The periosteal layer is the one attached to bone, so it must be on the outside against the skull.
Fibrous and synovial layers make up the articular capsule of a synovial joint. This would be the answer if the question asked about the layers of a joint capsule.
questions.answerText: An outer periosteal layer and an inner meningeal layer

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A ventricle is described as paired, with one chamber in each cerebral hemisphere. Which ventricle is it?
options: The fourth ventricle
The central canal
The third ventricle
The lateral ventricle
questions.why: The lateral ventricles are the only paired ventricles, one in each cerebral hemisphere, and they are the largest. They develop from the cavity of the telencephalon, the same embryonic region that forms the cerebrum. Each opens into the third ventricle through an interventricular foramen.
notes: The fourth ventricle is a single chamber between the brainstem and the cerebellum. It would be the answer for a question about the ventricle drained by the apertures.
The central canal is a single, unpaired channel through the spinal cord. Pick it if the question asked which CSF space lies inside the cord.
The third ventricle is a single midline chamber in the diencephalon. Pick it if the question asked which ventricle the thalami surround.
Correct. The lateral ventricles are paired, one per hemisphere.
questions.answerText: The lateral ventricle

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: After a head injury, blood collects in the potential space just beneath the dura, between the dura and the arachnoid. Which condition is this?
options: A subdural hematoma
An epidural hematoma
Hydrocephalus
A subarachnoid hemorrhage
questions.why: Sub means beneath, so a subdural hematoma is a collection of blood beneath the dura, in the subdural space between the dura and the arachnoid. That space is normally only a potential space, so the blood forces the two layers apart. Naming each bleed by its layers tells a clinician exactly where it is.
notes: Correct. Blood between the dura and arachnoid is a subdural hematoma.
An epidural hematoma sits outside the dura, between the dura and the skull. Pick it if the bleed lay above the dura rather than beneath it.
Hydrocephalus is a buildup of CSF in the ventricles, not a bleed between meninges. It would be the answer if the question described enlarged ventricles from blocked CSF flow.
A subarachnoid hemorrhage is bleeding into the CSF-filled space between the arachnoid and pia, one layer deeper. Pick it if the blood mixed into the CSF.
questions.answerText: A subdural hematoma

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which structure is a network of capillaries inside the ventricles that produces cerebrospinal fluid?
options: The cerebral aqueduct
An arachnoid granulation
The choroid plexus
A dural venous sinus
questions.why: The choroid plexus is a network of capillaries wrapped in ependymal cells. It is found in the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles, and it produces CSF from the blood plasma that passes through it. The fluid then flows through the ventricles and out to the subarachnoid space.
notes: The cerebral aqueduct is a narrow channel that carries CSF from the third to the fourth ventricle; it moves fluid but does not make it. Pick it for a question about the link between those ventricles.
An arachnoid granulation reabsorbs CSF into venous blood at the end of the circulation, the opposite job. Pick it if the question asked where CSF leaves the CNS.
Correct. The choroid plexus produces CSF.
A dural venous sinus is a channel in the dura that collects venous blood. It would be the answer if the question asked where the arachnoid granulations empty CSF.
questions.answerText: The choroid plexus

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which space lies between the spinal dura mater and the surrounding bone of the vertebral canal?
options: The subdural space
The epidural space
The subarachnoid space
The central canal
questions.why: The spinal dura is a single layer that is not attached to bone, so a true epidural space lies between it and the vertebrae. This space is filled with fat and veins. Inside the skull, by contrast, the periosteal dura is attached to the bone, so the cranial epidural space is only a potential space.
notes: The subdural space lies just deep to the dura, between it and the arachnoid. Pick it if the question asked which space lies beneath the dura.
Correct. The epidural space lies between the spinal dura and the vertebral bone.
The subarachnoid space lies deeper still, between the arachnoid and pia, and holds CSF. It would be the answer for where a lumbar puncture draws fluid.
The central canal is a channel inside the spinal cord, not a space around it. Pick it if the question asked which channel continues from the fourth ventricle.
questions.answerText: The epidural space

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which projections extend from the arachnoid mater into a dural sinus and return cerebrospinal fluid to the venous blood?
options: The denticulate ligaments
The cerebral aqueduct
The choroid plexus
The arachnoid granulations
questions.why: Arachnoid granulations are small projections of the arachnoid mater that push through the dura into the dural venous sinuses, mainly the superior sagittal sinus. CSF in the subarachnoid space passes through them into the venous blood. This reabsorption balances production, keeping the volume of CSF steady.
notes: The denticulate ligaments are tooth-like extensions of pia mater that anchor the spinal cord to the dura. Pick them if the question asked what holds the cord in place side to side.
The cerebral aqueduct is a channel between the third and fourth ventricles, not a projection into a sinus. It would be the answer for the link between those two ventricles.
The choroid plexus produces CSF in the ventricles rather than returning it to the blood. Pick it if the question asked where CSF is made.
Correct. Arachnoid granulations return CSF to the venous blood.
questions.answerText: The arachnoid granulations

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A patient has fever, headache, and a stiff neck, and tests show inflammation of the membranes that wrap the brain and spinal cord, caused by an infection. Which disorder is this?
options: Hydrocephalus
Meningitis
Encephalitis
Epidural hematoma
questions.why: Meningitis is inflammation of the meninges, the three connective tissue membranes around the brain and cord, usually caused by infection. The suffix itis means inflammation, and mening refers to the meninges. It is diagnosed by testing CSF drawn at a lumbar puncture, since the CSF flows between these membranes.
notes: Hydrocephalus is a buildup of CSF that enlarges the ventricles. Pick it if the question described enlarged ventricles and raised pressure from blocked CSF flow.
Correct. Infection and inflammation of the meninges is meningitis.
Encephalitis is inflammation of the brain tissue itself rather than its membranes. Pick it if the question described inflammation inside the brain.
An epidural hematoma is a collection of blood between the dura and the skull, not an infection. It would be the answer for a bleed outside the dura after a head injury.
questions.answerText: Meningitis

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A ventricle receives CSF from the cerebral aqueduct and passes it on to both the central canal and the subarachnoid space. Which ventricle is it?
options: The central canal
The fourth ventricle
A lateral ventricle
The third ventricle
questions.why: The fourth ventricle sits between the brainstem and cerebellum, at the end of the ventricular route. CSF arrives from the cerebral aqueduct and leaves through three apertures (two lateral and one median) into the subarachnoid space, with some passing down into the central canal of the cord. It is the only ventricle that opens to the subarachnoid space.
notes: The central canal receives some CSF from the fourth ventricle; it is not a ventricle that feeds the subarachnoid space. Pick it for a question about the channel through the spinal cord.
Correct. The fourth ventricle receives fluid from the aqueduct and opens to the central canal and subarachnoid space.
A lateral ventricle drains into the third ventricle through an interventricular foramen. It would be the answer if the question asked where CSF begins its route through the ventricles.
The third ventricle sends CSF into the cerebral aqueduct rather than receiving from it. Pick it if the question asked which ventricle drains into the aqueduct.
questions.answerText: The fourth ventricle

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which list orders the three meninges from the skull inward toward the brain surface?
options: Pia mater, arachnoid mater, dura mater
Dura mater, pia mater, arachnoid mater
Arachnoid mater, dura mater, pia mater
Dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater
questions.why: From the skull inward, the dura mater is the tough outer layer, the arachnoid mater is the delicate middle layer, and the pia mater is the thin inner layer clinging to the brain. The Latin names run from tough mother on the outside to tender mother within. The CSF-filled subarachnoid space lies between the arachnoid and the pia.
notes: This is the correct sequence read from the brain outward. Pick it only if the question asked for the order starting at the brain surface.
This places the pia between the dura and arachnoid. The pia always lies deepest, directly on the brain, with the subarachnoid space separating it from the arachnoid.
This puts the arachnoid outside the dura. The dura is always the outermost layer, against the skull.
Correct. Dura, arachnoid, then pia.
questions.answerText: Dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which list orders the ventricles in the direction cerebrospinal fluid flows through them?
options: Lateral ventricles, fourth ventricle, third ventricle
Fourth ventricle, third ventricle, lateral ventricles
Third ventricle, lateral ventricles, fourth ventricle
Lateral ventricles, third ventricle, fourth ventricle
questions.why: CSF made in the lateral ventricles flows through the interventricular foramina into the third ventricle. From there it runs down the cerebral aqueduct into the fourth ventricle, which then opens into the subarachnoid space and the central canal. The numbering of the ventricles matches the direction of flow.
notes: This skips past the third ventricle. The lateral ventricles connect only to the third ventricle, which then connects to the fourth.
This is the correct sequence read backward, against the direction of flow. Pick it only if the question asked for the order moving upstream.
This starts at the third ventricle. The lateral ventricles are upstream of the third, so fluid passes from lateral to third, not the reverse.
Correct. Lateral, third, then fourth.
questions.answerText: Lateral ventricles, third ventricle, fourth ventricle

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which list traces the circulation of cerebrospinal fluid in order, from production to reabsorption?
options: Arachnoid granulations, subarachnoid space, ventricles, choroid plexus
Choroid plexus, subarachnoid space, ventricles, arachnoid granulations
Choroid plexus, ventricles, subarachnoid space, arachnoid granulations
Ventricles, choroid plexus, arachnoid granulations, subarachnoid space
questions.why: The choroid plexus in the ventricles produces CSF, which flows through the ventricles and leaves the fourth ventricle through its apertures. It then bathes the brain and cord in the subarachnoid space and is reabsorbed at the arachnoid granulations into the venous blood of the superior sagittal sinus. The loop is one way, made inside the ventricles and reabsorbed outside them.
notes: This is the loop read backward, starting at reabsorption. Pick it only if the question asked for the order from reabsorption back to production.
This sends CSF to the subarachnoid space before the ventricles. The choroid plexus sits inside the ventricles, so fluid fills the ventricles first and only then reaches the subarachnoid space.
Correct. Choroid plexus, ventricles, subarachnoid space, then arachnoid granulations.
This reverses the last two steps and lists the ventricles before the choroid plexus that fills them. CSF reaches the subarachnoid space before it can be reabsorbed at the granulations.
questions.answerText: Choroid plexus, ventricles, subarachnoid space, arachnoid granulations

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Starting in a lateral ventricle, which list names, in order, the passages and chamber CSF moves through to reach the fourth ventricle?
options: Cerebral aqueduct, third ventricle, interventricular foramen
Interventricular foramen, cerebral aqueduct, third ventricle
Central canal, third ventricle, cerebral aqueduct
Interventricular foramen, third ventricle, cerebral aqueduct
questions.why: CSF leaves each lateral ventricle through an interventricular foramen (of Monro) and enters the third ventricle in the diencephalon. It then flows down the cerebral aqueduct through the midbrain and empties into the fourth ventricle. Each narrow passage on this route is a place where a blockage can back fluid up.
notes: This reverses the two passages. The aqueduct leads out of the third ventricle toward the fourth, so it comes last, not first.
This sends CSF into the aqueduct before the third ventricle. The aqueduct begins at the third ventricle, so fluid must pass through that ventricle first.

The central canal is in the spinal cord, below the fourth ventricle, so it cannot lie on the route from a lateral ventricle. Pick the central canal if the question asked where CSF goes after the fourth ventricle within the cord.
Correct. Interventricular foramen, third ventricle, then cerebral aqueduct.
questions.answerText: Interventricular foramen, third ventricle, cerebral aqueduct

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: In the vertebral canal, which list orders the three meningeal spaces from the vertebral bone inward toward the spinal cord?
options: Epidural space, subdural space, subarachnoid space
Subdural space, epidural space, subarachnoid space
Subarachnoid space, subdural space, epidural space
Epidural space, subarachnoid space, subdural space
questions.why: Each space is named for its position relative to a membrane. The epidural space lies outside the dura, against the bone, and holds fat and veins. The subdural space lies beneath the dura, between it and the arachnoid, and the subarachnoid space lies beneath the arachnoid, between it and the pia, holding CSF.
notes: Correct. Epidural, subdural, then subarachnoid.
This places the subdural space outside the epidural space. Epi means upon, so the epidural space is on the outside of the dura, next to bone.
This is the correct sequence read from the cord outward. Pick it only if the question asked for the order starting at the spinal cord.
This swaps the subdural and subarachnoid spaces. The subdural space lies just under the dura, so it comes before the space under the arachnoid.
questions.answerText: Epidural space, subdural space, subarachnoid space

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which dural reflection dips into the longitudinal fissure between the cerebral hemispheres?
options: The falx cerebri
The falx cerebelli
The filum terminale
The tentorium cerebelli
questions.why: The dural reflections are inward folds of the meningeal dura that partition the cranial cavity. The falx cerebri is a sickle-shaped fold that hangs down into the longitudinal fissure and separates the right and left cerebral hemispheres. The superior sagittal sinus runs along its top edge.
notes: Correct. The falx cerebri dips into the longitudinal fissure.
The falx cerebelli is a small fold that separates the right and left cerebellar hemispheres. Pick it if the question asked what divides the two halves of the cerebellum.
The filum terminale is a thread of pia mater, not dura, that anchors the lower end of the spinal cord to the coccyx. Pick it if the question asked what anchors the conus medullaris.
The tentorium cerebelli is a horizontal fold that separates the cerebrum above from the cerebellum below. It would be the answer for the fold lying in the transverse fissure.
questions.answerText: The falx cerebri

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which dural reflection separates the cerebrum above from the cerebellum below?
options: The falx cerebri
The falx cerebelli
The denticulate ligament
The tentorium cerebelli
questions.why: The tentorium cerebelli is a tent-like, roughly horizontal fold of meningeal dura that lies in the transverse fissure. It forms a roof over the cerebellum and supports the occipital lobes above it. Its name means tent of the cerebellum.
notes: The falx cerebri is a vertical fold that separates the right and left cerebral hemispheres in the longitudinal fissure. Pick it if the question asked what divides the two cerebral hemispheres.
The falx cerebelli is a small vertical fold between the right and left cerebellar hemispheres. It would be the answer for a fold that splits the cerebellum side to side.
The denticulate ligaments are tooth-like extensions of pia mater that anchor the spinal cord to the dura, not dural folds in the skull. Pick them if the question asked what holds the cord in place.
Correct. The tentorium cerebelli separates the cerebrum from the cerebellum.
questions.answerText: The tentorium cerebelli

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: How many ventricles does the brain have?
options: Five
Four
Three
Two
questions.why: The brain has four ventricles: the two lateral ventricles (one in each hemisphere), the third ventricle in the diencephalon, and the fourth ventricle between the brainstem and the cerebellum. They are connected in sequence and all contain choroid plexus. The central canal of the spinal cord is continuous with them but is not counted as a ventricle.
notes: Five comes from adding the central canal of the spinal cord to the four brain ventricles. The central canal is continuous with the fourth ventricle but is a separate channel in the cord.
Correct. The brain has four ventricles.
Three comes from counting the lateral ventricles as one chamber, or from leaving out one of the unpaired ventricles. Both lateral ventricles count separately.
Two is the number of lateral ventricles alone. Pick two if the question asked how many lateral ventricles there are.
questions.answerText: Four

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Where are the lateral ventricles located?
options: In the diencephalon
Between the brainstem and cerebellum
One in each cerebral hemisphere
Within the spinal cord
questions.why: The lateral ventricles are a pair of large, curved chambers, one inside each cerebral hemisphere. They hold choroid plexus and are where CSF circulation begins. Each opens into the third ventricle through an interventricular foramen.
notes: The diencephalon encloses the third ventricle. Pick this location if the question asked where the third ventricle sits.
The fourth ventricle lies between the brainstem and the cerebellum. This location would be the answer for the fourth ventricle.
Correct. There is one lateral ventricle in each hemisphere.
The central canal runs within the spinal cord. Pick this location if the question asked about the CSF channel continuous with the fourth ventricle.
questions.answerText: One in each cerebral hemisphere

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which meningeal space is found in the vertebral canal but not normally inside the cranium?
options: The epidural space
The lumbar cistern
The subarachnoid space
The subdural space
questions.why: In the cranium, the outer periosteal layer of the dura is attached to the skull, so the epidural space there is only a potential space that opens if something, such as blood, separates the dura from the bone. In the vertebral canal, the spinal dura is a single layer that is not fused to bone, which leaves a true epidural space filled with fat and veins. This is why epidural injections are given in the back.
notes: Correct. The epidural space is a real space in the vertebral canal but only a potential space in the cranium.

The lumbar cistern is also found only in the vertebral canal, but it is part of the subarachnoid space rather than a separate meningeal space. Pick it if the question asked where a spinal tap draws CSF.
The subarachnoid space surrounds both the brain and the cord and holds CSF at both sites. It would be the answer if the question asked which space is continuous from the brain down to the cord.
The subdural space, a potential space between the dura and arachnoid, exists both in the cranium and in the vertebral canal. Pick it if the question asked where a subdural hematoma forms.
questions.answerText: The epidural space

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which tooth-like extensions of pia mater anchor the spinal cord to the dura along its length?
options: The denticulate ligaments
The dural reflections
The arachnoid granulations
The filum terminale
questions.why: The denticulate ligaments are extensions of pia mater that project from each side of the spinal cord and attach to the dura. They hold the cord in the middle of the vertebral canal so it does not shift side to side. Denticulate means tooth-like, which describes their pointed shape.
notes: Correct. The denticulate ligaments anchor the cord to the dura along its sides.
The dural reflections are folds of dura inside the skull, such as the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli. Pick them if the question asked what partitions the cranial cavity.
The arachnoid granulations are projections of the arachnoid into the dural sinuses that reabsorb CSF. Pick them if the question asked where CSF returns to the blood.

The filum terminale is also made of pia mater, but it is a single thread that runs down from the conus medullaris to the coccyx. It would be the answer if the question asked what anchors the lower end of the cord.
questions.answerText: The denticulate ligaments

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which glial cells line the ventricles and the central canal?
options: Oligodendrocytes
Microglia
Astrocytes
Ependymal cells
questions.why: Ependymal cells are glial cells that form the lining of the ventricles and the central canal of the spinal cord. They also wrap the capillaries of the choroid plexus, where CSF is produced, and they help circulate the fluid. Their position on the walls of the fluid spaces is the clue to their identity.
notes: Oligodendrocytes form the myelin sheaths around axons in the CNS. They would be the answer if the question asked which cells myelinate CNS axons.
Microglia are small phagocytic glia that clean up debris and microbes in the CNS. Pick them if the question asked which glia act as the immune defense of the brain.
Astrocytes are star-shaped glia whose end-feet wrap brain capillaries and help form the blood-brain barrier. Pick them if the question asked which glia contribute to that barrier.
Correct. Ependymal cells line the ventricles and central canal.
questions.answerText: Ependymal cells

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: What is the enlarged, CSF-filled part of the subarachnoid space below the conus medullaris called?
options: The central canal
The cisterna chyli
The lumbar cistern
The epidural space
questions.why: Because the spinal cord ends near the L1 to L2 disc while the subarachnoid space continues lower, a large pool of CSF lies below the conus medullaris. This pool is the lumbar cistern, and only the floating roots of the cauda equina lie within it. It is the target of a lumbar puncture.
notes: The central canal is inside the spinal cord itself, so it ends with the cord rather than continuing below it. It would be the answer for the CSF channel continuous with the fourth ventricle.
The cisterna chyli is a lymphatic sac in the abdomen that collects lymph at the start of the thoracic duct. The similar name is the trap; pick it for a question about where the thoracic duct begins.
Correct. The lumbar cistern is the CSF pool below the conus medullaris.
The epidural space lies outside the dura and holds fat and veins rather than CSF. Pick it if the question asked where an epidural anesthetic is placed.
questions.answerText: The lumbar cistern

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A bleed collects between the dura mater and the skull. Which type of bleed is this?
options: A dural sinus clot
A subdural hematoma
A subarachnoid hemorrhage
An epidural hematoma
questions.why: A bleed between the dura and the skull lies on the outside of the dura, so it is called an epidural hematoma, from epi meaning upon. Because the cranial dura is normally attached to bone, the blood must strip the dura away from the skull as it collects. Each named bleed is identified by the layers on either side of it.
notes: A clot inside a dural venous sinus blocks venous drainage within the dura rather than forming a pool of blood outside it. Pick it if the question described a blocked sinus such as the superior sagittal sinus.
A subdural hematoma lies beneath the dura, between the dura and the arachnoid. Pick it if the bleed were one layer deeper.
A subarachnoid hemorrhage is bleeding into the CSF-filled space between the arachnoid and pia. It would be the answer if the blood mixed with the CSF around the brain.
Correct. Blood between the dura and the skull is an epidural hematoma.
questions.answerText: An epidural hematoma

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which meningeal space lies between the arachnoid mater and the pia mater?
options: The central canal
The subdural space
The subarachnoid space
The epidural space
questions.why: The subarachnoid space lies beneath the arachnoid mater and above the pia mater, which is how it gets its name. It is a real space, crossed by the arachnoid's web-like strands and filled with CSF. Below the end of the spinal cord it widens into the lumbar cistern.
notes: The central canal is a channel inside the spinal cord, deep to all the meninges. Pick it if the question asked which CSF space lies within the cord itself.
The subdural space lies between the dura and the arachnoid, one layer more superficial. It would be the answer if the question asked which space lies just beneath the dura.
Correct. The subarachnoid space lies between the arachnoid and pia.
The epidural space lies outside the dura, between the spinal dura and the vertebral bone. Pick it if the question asked which space lies outside all three meninges.
questions.answerText: The subarachnoid space

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which structure separates the right and left cerebellar hemispheres?
options: The tentorium cerebelli
The falx cerebelli
The vermis
The falx cerebri
questions.why: The falx cerebelli is a small vertical fold of meningeal dura that projects between the right and left cerebellar hemispheres. It is the cerebellar counterpart of the falx cerebri, which separates the cerebral hemispheres. Falx means sickle, describing the curved shape of both folds.
notes: The tentorium cerebelli separates the cerebrum above from the cerebellum below. It would be the answer for the horizontal fold over the cerebellum.
Correct. The falx cerebelli separates the cerebellar hemispheres.

The vermis is the narrow midline band of cerebellar tissue that connects the two cerebellar hemispheres; it joins them rather than separating them. Pick it if the question asked what links the cerebellar hemispheres.
The falx cerebri separates the right and left cerebral hemispheres, not the cerebellar ones. Pick it if the question asked what fills the longitudinal fissure.
questions.answerText: The falx cerebelli

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Through which openings does CSF leave the fourth ventricle to enter the subarachnoid space?
options: The apertures of the fourth ventricle
The arachnoid granulations in the sinus
The interventricular foramina
The cerebral aqueduct
questions.why: The fourth ventricle has three apertures: two lateral apertures (of Luschka) and one median aperture (of Magendie). Through them, CSF leaves the ventricular system and enters the subarachnoid space around the brain and cord. These are the only openings from the ventricles to the outside of the brain.
notes: Correct. CSF exits through the lateral and median apertures of the fourth ventricle.
The arachnoid granulations are where CSF leaves the subarachnoid space and returns to the venous blood, a later step. Pick them for a question about reabsorption.
The interventricular foramina connect the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle, at the start of the route. Pick them if the question asked how CSF reaches the third ventricle.
The cerebral aqueduct brings CSF into the fourth ventricle from the third, rather than letting it out. It would be the answer if the question asked how CSF reaches the fourth ventricle.
questions.answerText: The apertures of the fourth ventricle

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: How does the spinal dura mater differ from the cranial dura mater?
options: It is a single layer not fused to bone
It has two layers fused to the vertebrae
It is the innermost layer, on the cord itself
It forms dural venous sinuses along the cord
questions.why: The cranial dura has two layers, an outer periosteal layer attached to the skull and an inner meningeal layer. The spinal dura is a single tough layer that is not attached to the vertebrae. That gap between the spinal dura and bone is the epidural space, a real space in the vertebral canal but only a potential space in the cranium.
notes: Correct. The spinal dura is a single layer that is not fused to bone.
This describes the cranial dura, which has two layers with the periosteal layer attached to the skull. Pick it if the question asked about the dura around the brain.
The dura is the outermost meninx at every level. The layer on the surface of the cord is the pia mater, so this is a mix-up between dura and pia.
The dural venous sinuses form only in the cranium, where the two dural layers separate. The single-layered spinal dura has no second layer to split.
questions.answerText: It is a single layer not fused to bone

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which three components build the blood-brain barrier?
options: Endothelium, basement membrane, astrocyte end-feet
The dura, the arachnoid, and the pia mater
Ependymal cells, the choroid plexus, and the pia mater
Microglia, oligodendrocytes, and Schwann cell sheaths
questions.why: The blood-brain barrier is the seal that controls what passes from the blood into brain tissue. Its first layer is the endothelial cells lining brain capillaries, joined by tight junctions and lacking the pores of ordinary capillaries. These cells sit on a basement membrane and are wrapped by the end-feet of astrocytes, which help control the barrier.
notes: Correct. Endothelium, basement membrane, and astrocyte end-feet form the blood-brain barrier.
These are the three meninges, the membranes around the brain and cord. They would be the answer if the question asked which connective tissue layers wrap the CNS.
These are structures that make and line the CSF spaces, not the barrier around brain capillaries. Pick them if the question asked what produces CSF.

Microglia clean up debris, oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons, and Schwann cells myelinate PNS axons; none of them forms the barrier. Pick oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells for a question about which cells make myelin.
questions.answerText: Endothelium, basement membrane, astrocyte end-feet

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A buildup of CSF that enlarges the ventricles and raises intracranial pressure is called what?
options: Hydrocephalus
Meningitis
A subdural hematoma
An epidural hematoma
questions.why: Hydrocephalus means water on the brain. It occurs when CSF is made faster than it can flow out or be reabsorbed, so fluid builds up and the ventricles enlarge. Because the adult skull cannot expand, the extra fluid raises intracranial pressure and compresses the brain.
notes: Correct. A CSF buildup that enlarges the ventricles is hydrocephalus.
Meningitis is inflammation of the meninges, usually from infection, not a buildup of CSF. Pick it if the question described an infection diagnosed by testing CSF.
A subdural hematoma is a collection of blood between the dura and the arachnoid. Pick it if the question described a bleed just beneath the dura.
An epidural hematoma is a collection of blood between the dura and the skull. It would be the answer for a bleed outside the dura.
questions.answerText: Hydrocephalus

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A patient needs CSF drawn for testing. The needle is placed in the midline between the L3 and L4 spinous processes. Which CSF-filled space is the target?
options: The subdural space
The epidural space
The lumbar cistern
The central canal
questions.why: The spinal cord ends at the conus medullaris near the L1 to L2 disc, but the subarachnoid space continues lower as the lumbar cistern, a pool of CSF holding only the floating cauda equina. A needle between L3 and L4 reaches this pool safely below the end of the cord. This mismatch between cord and column is the whole basis of the lumbar puncture.
notes: The subdural space is only a potential space between the dura and arachnoid with no pool of CSF. It would be the answer if the question asked where a subdural hematoma collects.
The epidural space is passed on the way in, but it holds fat and veins rather than CSF. Pick it if the question asked where an epidural anesthetic is delivered.
Correct. A lumbar puncture targets the lumbar cistern.
The central canal is inside the spinal cord, which ends near L1 to L2, so it is not present at L3 to L4. Puncturing the cord is exactly what the low needle position avoids.
questions.answerText: The lumbar cistern

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A clinician suspects meningitis and orders a lumbar puncture. Which structure is inflamed in meningitis?
options: The epidural space
The ventricles
The choroid plexus
The meninges
questions.why: Meningitis is inflammation of the meninges, the three connective tissue membranes that wrap the brain and spinal cord, usually caused by infection. Because CSF flows in the subarachnoid space between two of these membranes, signs of the infection show up in the CSF. That is why a lumbar puncture is used to diagnose it.
notes: The epidural space is a space filled with fat and veins outside the spinal dura, not a membrane, so it is not what meningitis inflames. It would be the answer for where an epidural injection is placed.
The ventricles are fluid-filled chambers inside the brain, not the membranes around it. They are the structures that enlarge in hydrocephalus.
The choroid plexus is the capillary tuft inside the ventricles that makes CSF, not a covering membrane. Pick it if the question asked where CSF is made.
Correct. Meningitis is inflammation of the meninges.
questions.answerText: The meninges

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: During a lumbar puncture, after crossing the epidural space, the needle pierces the tough outer meningeal membrane. Which membrane is this?
options: The ligamentum flavum
The pia mater
The arachnoid mater
The dura mater
questions.why: A lumbar puncture needle passes through skin, fat, three ligaments, and the epidural space before meeting the meninges. The first membrane it pierces is the dura mater, the tough outer layer. It then passes the delicate arachnoid mater and enters the subarachnoid space, where CSF is withdrawn.
notes: The ligamentum flavum is the tough elastic ligament crossed before the epidural space, not a meningeal membrane. Pick it if the question asked which ligament a clinician feels give way just before the epidural space.
The pia mater clings to the surface of the cord and nerve roots, deep to the CSF, so the needle does not need to reach it. Pick it if the question asked which layer lies directly on the cord.
The arachnoid mater is pierced right after the dura, just before the needle reaches CSF, and it is delicate rather than tough. It would be the answer for the last membrane crossed before CSF appears.
Correct. The needle pierces the dura mater after the epidural space.
questions.answerText: The dura mater

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: At the arachnoid granulations, CSF is reabsorbed mainly into the venous blood of which dural sinus?
options: The confluence of sinuses
The superior sagittal sinus
The internal jugular vein
The sigmoid sinus
questions.why: The superior sagittal sinus runs along the top edge of the falx cerebri, in the midline at the top of the skull. Arachnoid granulations push up into this sinus, and CSF passes through them into its venous blood, completing the CSF loop. The blood then drains back toward the heart through the other sinuses and the internal jugular veins.
notes: The confluence of sinuses is the meeting point of the major sinuses at the internal occipital protuberance, downstream of the superior sagittal sinus. It would be the answer if the question asked where the superior sagittal sinus empties.
Correct. CSF is reabsorbed mainly into the superior sagittal sinus.

The internal jugular vein is not a dural sinus; it carries blood out of the skull after the sinuses drain into it. Pick it if the question asked which vessel takes venous blood from the brain back toward the heart.

The sigmoid sinuses are S-shaped sinuses that carry blood down toward the jugular foramen, near the end of the drainage route. Pick them if the question asked which sinuses lead into the internal jugular veins.
questions.answerText: The superior sagittal sinus

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the three meninges?
options: Dura is lace-like and middle; arachnoid is tough and outer; pia is thin and on the brain
Dura is thin and on the brain; arachnoid is tough and outer; pia is lace-like and middle
Dura is tough and outer; pia is lace-like and middle; arachnoid is thin and on the brain
Dura is tough and outer; arachnoid is lace-like and middle; pia is thin and on the brain
questions.why: The meninges protect the CNS in layers. The dura mater is a tough outer membrane of dense connective tissue, the arachnoid mater is a delicate, lace-like middle membrane, and the pia mater is a thin, vascular inner membrane that clings to the surface of the brain and cord. The CSF-filled subarachnoid space between the arachnoid and pia adds a cushion of fluid.
notes: This swaps the dura and arachnoid. The dura is the tough outermost layer, and the arachnoid is the delicate middle layer.
This swaps every description. The dura is the tough outer layer, not the thin inner one, and the pia is the thin layer on the brain.
This swaps the arachnoid and pia. The pia is the layer that clings to the brain, and the arachnoid is the lace-like layer in the middle.
Correct. Dura tough and outer, arachnoid lace-like and middle, pia thin and on the brain.
questions.answerText: Dura is tough and outer; arachnoid is lace-like and middle; pia is thin and on the brain

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Cerebrospinal fluid is made and reabsorbed continuously. Besides cushioning and floating the brain, which job does this circulating fluid do for the neurons it bathes?
options: It carries nutrients to them and removes their wastes
It insulates their axons so signals travel faster
It collects venous blood and drains it toward the heart
It screens what passes from the blood into brain tissue
questions.why: Besides buoyancy and protection, CSF provides chemical stability. As it circulates, it carries nutrients, removes wastes, and keeps a steady environment around the neurons. Constant production at the choroid plexus and reabsorption at the arachnoid granulations keep the fluid fresh.
notes: Correct. CSF carries nutrients and removes wastes, keeping the neurons' surroundings stable.
Insulating axons is the job of myelin, made by oligodendrocytes in the CNS and Schwann cells in the PNS. Pick this if the question asked what myelin does.
Collecting venous blood is the job of the dural venous sinuses. This would be the answer if the question asked what the superior sagittal sinus does.

Screening what enters brain tissue from the blood is the job of the blood-brain barrier, built from capillary endothelium, basement membrane, and astrocyte end-feet. Pick this for a question about the BBB.
questions.answerText: It carries nutrients to them and removes their wastes

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which property of cerebrospinal fluid keeps the brain from crushing its own lower structures under its own weight?
options: Chemical stability, which keeps the neurons' fluid steady
Waste removal, which clears metabolic products from tissue
Cushioning, which absorbs the force of sudden blows
Buoyancy, which floats the brain and lightens its load
questions.why: Because the brain floats in CSF, the fluid supports most of its weight, so its effective weight is far lower than its weight in air. Without that support, the brain would press down on its own base. Buoyancy is one of three roles of CSF, along with protection against blows and chemical stability.
notes: Chemical stability is a real role of CSF, keeping the environment around neurons steady, but it does not support weight. It would be the answer for a question about the fluid's chemical job.
Waste removal is part of the chemical role of CSF and has nothing to do with supporting the brain's weight. Pick it if the question asked why CSF must circulate and be replaced.
Cushioning is a real role of CSF, but it protects against jolts and blows to the head, not against the brain's constant weight. Pick it if the question asked how CSF protects the brain in a fall.
Correct. Buoyancy floats the brain and keeps it from crushing its base.
questions.answerText: Buoyancy, which floats the brain and lightens its load

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: CSF drawn from the lower back can reveal an infection or bleed around the brain. Which anatomical fact explains this?
options: The central canal carries blood down from the brain to the cord
The subarachnoid space is continuous around the brain and cord
The lumbar cistern drains directly into the dural sinuses
The epidural space holds CSF that drains from the brain
questions.why: The subarachnoid space is one continuous space that surrounds the whole brain and spinal cord, and the lumbar cistern is simply its lowest part. The same CSF circulates through all of it, so blood or infection near the brain shows up in fluid sampled from the lumbar cistern. This is why a lumbar puncture is used to diagnose meningitis and subarachnoid hemorrhage.
notes: The central canal carries CSF, not blood, and it runs inside the cord, which ends above the lumbar puncture site. Pick the central canal for a question about the CSF channel continuous with the fourth ventricle.
Correct. The subarachnoid space is continuous around the brain and cord.

CSF drains into the dural sinuses at the arachnoid granulations, mainly into the superior sagittal sinus at the top of the skull, not from the lumbar cistern. Pick the granulations if the question asked where CSF is reabsorbed.
The epidural space holds fat and veins, not CSF, and it lies outside the dura. It would be the answer if the question asked where an epidural anesthetic is placed.
questions.answerText: The subarachnoid space is continuous around the brain and cord

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: The dura mater is the toughest of the meninges. Which tissue type is it built from?
options: Simple squamous epithelium
Hyaline cartilage
Areolar connective tissue
Dense connective tissue
questions.why: The dura mater is a tough membrane of dense connective tissue, packed with collagen fibers that resist stretching and tearing. Its strength suits its position as the outermost protective layer against the skull and vertebral canal. The thinner arachnoid and pia are more delicate connective tissue layers.
notes: Simple squamous epithelium is a single layer of flat cells, such as the lining of blood vessels and alveoli. Pick it if the question asked what tissue lines the capillaries of the blood-brain barrier.
Hyaline cartilage is a firm, glassy tissue found on joint surfaces and in the costal cartilages. It would be the answer for a question about the tissue covering the ends of long bones.

Areolar connective tissue is loose tissue with widely spaced fibers that fills spaces under epithelia. It would be the answer if the question asked what tissue packs loosely around organs and vessels.
Correct. The dura is built from dense connective tissue.
questions.answerText: Dense connective tissue

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A child's scan shows enlarged lateral ventricles and an enlarged third ventricle, but a normal-sized fourth ventricle. Where is the CSF most likely blocked?
options: At one interventricular foramen
At the arachnoid granulations
At the cerebral aqueduct
At the apertures of the fourth ventricle
questions.why: CSF backs up behind a blockage, so every chamber upstream enlarges and every chamber downstream stays normal. The lateral and third ventricles are upstream of the cerebral aqueduct, while the fourth ventricle lies downstream of it. The aqueduct is a narrow channel through the midbrain, which makes it a common site of blockage.
notes: A blocked interventricular foramen would trap fluid in only one lateral ventricle, leaving the third ventricle normal. Pick it if the scan showed just one enlarged lateral ventricle.
Poor reabsorption at the arachnoid granulations would back fluid up through the whole system, including the fourth ventricle. Pick it if every ventricle and the subarachnoid space were enlarged.
Correct. A blocked cerebral aqueduct enlarges the lateral and third ventricles but spares the fourth.
Blocked apertures would trap CSF inside all the ventricles, so the fourth ventricle would enlarge too. This would be the answer if all four ventricles were enlarged.
questions.answerText: At the cerebral aqueduct

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: If CSF production continued normally but reabsorption at the arachnoid granulations were blocked, which condition would result?
options: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
Hydrocephalus
Subdural hematoma
Meningitis
questions.why: CSF volume stays steady only when reabsorption keeps pace with production. If the arachnoid granulations cannot return fluid to the venous blood, CSF accumulates, the ventricles enlarge, and pressure inside the rigid skull rises. That buildup of CSF is hydrocephalus.
notes: A subarachnoid hemorrhage is bleeding into the CSF-filled space around the brain. Pick it if the question described blood mixing into the CSF.
Correct. Blocked reabsorption causes CSF to build up, which is hydrocephalus.
A subdural hematoma is bleeding between the dura and arachnoid, usually from trauma, not a buildup of CSF. Pick it if the question described blood collecting beneath the dura.
Meningitis is inflammation of the meninges, usually from infection. It would be the answer if the question described an infection found by testing CSF.
questions.answerText: Hydrocephalus

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which thread of pia mater extends from the conus medullaris and anchors the lower end of the spinal cord to the coccyx?
options: The filum terminale
The cauda equina
The ligamentum flavum
The denticulate ligament
questions.why: The filum terminale is a slender thread of pia mater that continues down from the conus medullaris, through the lumbar cistern, and anchors on the coccyx. It holds the lower end of the cord in place. Its name means terminal thread, because it begins where the cord ends.
notes: Correct. The filum terminale anchors the cord to the coccyx.
The cauda equina is a bundle of many nerve roots below the conus, not a single anchoring thread of pia. It would be the answer if the question asked what nerve roots hang in the lumbar cistern.

The ligamentum flavum is an elastic ligament joining the laminae of adjacent vertebrae, outside the dura. Pick it if the question asked which ligament a lumbar puncture needle passes just before the epidural space.

The denticulate ligaments are also extensions of pia mater, but they project from the sides of the cord along its length and attach to the dura. Pick them if the question asked what anchors the cord side to side.
questions.answerText: The filum terminale

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Venous blood from the brain flows through the dural sinuses and leaves the skull. The sigmoid sinuses drain directly into which vessels?
options: The internal jugular veins
The transverse sinuses
The external jugular veins
The vertebral arteries
questions.why: The main drainage route runs from the superior sagittal sinus to the confluence of sinuses, then out through the paired transverse sinuses to the S-shaped sigmoid sinuses. The sigmoid sinuses curve down to the jugular foramen and become the internal jugular veins. These veins carry the blood out of the skull and back toward the heart.
notes: Correct. The sigmoid sinuses drain into the internal jugular veins.
The transverse sinuses come before the sigmoid sinuses, carrying blood from the confluence out to them. They would be the answer if the question asked what drains into the sigmoid sinuses.
The external jugular veins drain the scalp and face on the outside of the neck, not the dural sinuses. Pick them if the question asked which superficial neck vein drains the face.
The vertebral arteries bring blood up to the brain rather than draining it, and they unite to form the basilar artery. Pick them if the question asked which arteries supply the posterior circulation.
questions.answerText: The internal jugular veins

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: During a lumbar puncture, which tough elastic ligament joining the laminae of adjacent vertebrae does the needle pass just before entering the epidural space?
options: The interspinous ligament
The ligamentum flavum
The denticulate ligament
The supraspinous ligament
questions.why: From superficial to deep, a lumbar puncture needle crosses the skin, subcutaneous fat, the supraspinous ligament, the interspinous ligament, and then the ligamentum flavum before entering the epidural space. The ligamentum flavum is tough and elastic, and clinicians feel it give way as a landmark. Flavum means yellow, from the color of its elastic fibers.
notes: The interspinous ligament lies between adjacent spinous processes and is crossed second, before the ligamentum flavum. It would be the answer for the ligament between the supraspinous ligament and the ligamentum flavum.
Correct. The ligamentum flavum is the last ligament before the epidural space.

The denticulate ligaments are extensions of pia mater inside the dura that anchor the cord, so the needle does not pass them on the way to the epidural space. Pick them if the question asked what holds the cord to the dura.
The supraspinous ligament runs along the tips of the spinous processes and is the first ligament the needle meets. Pick it if the question asked which ligament lies most superficially.
questions.answerText: The ligamentum flavum

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: What fills the epidural space of the vertebral canal?
options: A thin film of fluid only
Arachnoid strands and CSF
Fat and veins
Cerebrospinal fluid
questions.why: The epidural space lies between the spinal dura and the vertebral bone, and it is filled with fat and a network of veins. The fat cushions the dural sac inside the bony canal. This is the space where an epidural anesthetic is injected, outside the dura, so the needle does not enter the CSF-filled subarachnoid space.
notes: A thin film of fluid describes the subdural space, which is only a potential space between the dura and arachnoid. It would be the answer for the subdural space.
Web-like arachnoid strands crossing a CSF-filled space describe the subarachnoid space. Pick this if the question asked about the space beneath the arachnoid.
Correct. The epidural space holds fat and veins.
CSF fills the subarachnoid space, which lies inside the dura and arachnoid. Pick CSF if the question asked what fills the subarachnoid space or lumbar cistern.
questions.answerText: Fat and veins

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A patient has bleeding directly into the CSF-filled space between the arachnoid and the pia. What is this called?
options: A subdural hematoma
Hydrocephalus
A subarachnoid hemorrhage
An epidural hematoma
questions.why: Bleeding into the subarachnoid space is a subarachnoid hemorrhage. Because that space holds CSF, the blood mixes into the fluid instead of forming a separate pool, and it can be detected in CSF drawn at a lumbar puncture. The bleed is named for the space it fills, beneath the arachnoid.
notes: A subdural hematoma is bleeding between the dura and arachnoid, one space more superficial. It would be the answer if the blood collected just beneath the dura.
Hydrocephalus is a buildup of CSF in the ventricles, not bleeding. Pick it if the question described enlarged ventricles from blocked CSF flow.
Correct. Bleeding into the subarachnoid space is a subarachnoid hemorrhage.
An epidural hematoma is bleeding between the dura and the skull, outside all the meninges. Pick it if the bleed lay above the dura.
questions.answerText: A subarachnoid hemorrhage

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: How do the endothelial cells of brain capillaries differ from those of ordinary capillaries, helping form the blood-brain barrier?
options: They are full of pores that let solutes pass freely
They are lined on the inside by ependymal cells
They are joined by tight junctions and lack pores
They are wrapped in myelin from oligodendrocytes
questions.why: In most capillaries, small gaps or pores let substances leak from the blood into the tissue. The endothelial cells of brain capillaries are sealed together by tight junctions and lack those pores, so substances must pass through the cells themselves. A basement membrane and astrocyte end-feet surround these capillaries to complete the barrier.
notes: Pores that let solutes pass freely describe leaky capillaries elsewhere in the body, such as in the kidney. This is the opposite of what the blood-brain barrier needs.
Ependymal cells line the ventricles and the central canal, not the inside of blood vessels. Pick them if the question asked what lines the CSF-filled cavities.
Correct. Tight junctions and the absence of pores seal brain capillaries.
Myelin wraps axons, not capillaries; oligodendrocytes make it in the CNS. Pick myelin if the question asked what speeds signals along CNS axons.
questions.answerText: They are joined by tight junctions and lack pores

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Where in the brain is the choroid plexus found?
options: In the fourth ventricle and central canal
In the lateral ventricles only
In the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles
In the subarachnoid space and lumbar cistern
questions.why: The choroid plexus, the capillary network that produces CSF, is found in all of the brain's ventricles: the lateral ventricles, the third ventricle, and the fourth ventricle. As CSF flows from one ventricle to the next, each one adds more fluid. CSF is then reabsorbed outside the ventricles, at the arachnoid granulations.
notes: The fourth ventricle has choroid plexus, but the central canal of the cord does not. This option misses the lateral and third ventricles and adds a channel that only carries CSF.
The lateral ventricles do hold choroid plexus and are where CSF production starts, but the third and fourth ventricles have it too. A student who thinks CSF comes from one place picks this.
Correct. Choroid plexus is in the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles.
The subarachnoid space and lumbar cistern hold CSF after it leaves the ventricles, but no choroid plexus lies there. Pick them if the question asked where CSF surrounds the brain and cord.
questions.answerText: In the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: The ring of arteries at the base of the brain that joins the anterior and posterior circulations is commonly called what?
options: The basilar artery
The confluence of sinuses
The Circle of Willis
The choroid plexus
questions.why: The cerebral arterial circle, usually called the Circle of Willis, is a ring of connected arteries under the brain. It links the internal carotid supply in front with the vertebral and basilar supply behind through the communicating arteries. Because it is a ring, blood can sometimes take another route if one vessel narrows slowly.
notes: The basilar artery is a single vessel formed by the two vertebral arteries, running up the front of the pons. It feeds the back of the ring, so it would be the answer for the artery that supplies the brainstem.

The confluence of sinuses is where the major dural venous sinuses meet at the internal occipital protuberance. It drains venous blood, so pick it for a question about where the superior sagittal and transverse sinuses join.
Correct. The cerebral arterial circle at the base of the brain is commonly called the Circle of Willis.
The choroid plexus is a network of capillaries inside the ventricles that produces cerebrospinal fluid. Choose it if the question asks where CSF is made.
questions.answerText: The Circle of Willis

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which cerebral artery supplies the lateral surface of the cerebrum, including much of the motor and sensory cortex for the body?
options: The anterior cerebral artery
The middle cerebral artery
The posterior cerebral artery
The basilar artery
questions.why: The internal carotid artery divides into the anterior and middle cerebral arteries. The middle cerebral artery is the larger branch, and it runs out through the lateral sulcus to supply the lateral surface of the cerebrum. That territory includes most of the primary motor and somatosensory cortex for the body, so a blockage here often causes weakness and numbness on the opposite side.
notes: The anterior cerebral artery supplies the medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes. Pick it for a question about blood supply to the inner surface of the hemisphere along the longitudinal fissure.
Correct. The middle cerebral artery feeds the lateral surface of the cerebrum.
The posterior cerebral artery supplies the occipital lobe and the inferior surface of the temporal lobe. It would be the answer for a stroke that causes loss of vision.
The basilar artery is formed by the two vertebral arteries and supplies the brainstem. Choose it for a question about the posterior circulation to the pons.
questions.answerText: The middle cerebral artery

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which two arteries unite to form the basilar artery?
options: The posterior communicating arteries
The vertebral arteries
The posterior cerebral arteries
The internal carotid arteries
questions.why: The two vertebral arteries travel up through the transverse foramina of the cervical vertebrae, enter the skull through the foramen magnum, and join on the front of the brainstem to form the single basilar artery. The basilar artery then runs up the pons and supplies the brainstem and cerebellum. This vertebral and basilar system is the posterior circulation of the brain.
notes: The posterior communicating arteries join each internal carotid to a posterior cerebral artery, linking the front and back of the Circle of Willis. Choose them for a question about that link.
Correct. The two vertebral arteries unite to form the basilar artery.
The posterior cerebral arteries are the branches at the top end of the basilar artery, not the vessels that form it. They would be the answer for the arteries supplying the occipital lobe.
The internal carotid arteries form the anterior circulation and divide into the anterior and middle cerebral arteries. Pick them if the question asks which vessels feed most of the cerebrum.
questions.answerText: The vertebral arteries

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: A slowly narrowing internal carotid artery causes few symptoms because blood reaches its territory through other vessels. Which structure makes this rerouting possible?
options: The middle cerebral artery
The Circle of Willis
The anterior spinal artery
The superior sagittal sinus
questions.why: The Circle of Willis is an anastomosis, a ring of connected arteries at the base of the brain that joins the anterior and posterior circulations through the communicating arteries. If one internal carotid artery narrows, blood can cross the ring from the other internal carotid or from the vertebral and basilar system. That alternate route keeps blood flowing to the territory of the narrowed artery.
notes: The middle cerebral artery is a single branch of the internal carotid that feeds the lateral cerebrum. It is a common site of blockage, not a ring that reroutes blood, so choose it for the artery supplying the motor and sensory cortex.
Correct. The Circle of Willis lets blood cross from one circulation to another when a vessel narrows.

The anterior spinal artery is a single midline vessel formed from both vertebral arteries that runs down the front of the spinal cord. It would be the answer for a question about blood supply to the anterior cord.

The superior sagittal sinus is a dural venous sinus that drains blood and CSF away from the brain. It carries venous blood out, so pick it for a question about where arachnoid granulations return CSF.
questions.answerText: The Circle of Willis

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: The brain floats in cerebrospinal fluid inside the skull. How does this fluid protect the brain?
options: It insulates the axons so that signals travel faster
It filters harmful substances out of the blood
It buoys the brain and cushions it against blows
It anchors the brain firmly against the skull
questions.why: Cerebrospinal fluid fills the subarachnoid space around the brain and spinal cord. Floating in it greatly reduces the brain's effective weight, so the soft tissue does not crush its own base. The fluid also acts as a liquid cushion that spreads out the force of a jolt or blow before the brain strikes bone.
notes: Insulating axons to speed signals is the job of the myelin sheath, made by oligodendrocytes in the CNS. Pick this idea for a question about why white matter conducts quickly.
Screening what passes from the blood into brain tissue is the job of the blood-brain barrier, built from tight capillary walls and astrocyte end-feet. Choose it for a question about that barrier.
Correct. CSF provides buoyancy and a shock-absorbing cushion around the brain.

CSF lets the brain float rather than pressing it against bone. Anchoring is done by structures such as the dural folds around the brain and the denticulate ligaments along the spinal cord, so pick those for a question about holding the CNS in place.
questions.answerText: It buoys the brain and cushions it against blows

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which statement best describes the main job of the blood-brain barrier?
options: It returns cerebrospinal fluid to the venous blood
It limits what passes from blood into brain tissue
It cushions the brain against sudden blows to the head
It produces cerebrospinal fluid from blood plasma
questions.why: Neurons need a stable chemical environment, but the chemistry of the blood changes constantly. The blood-brain barrier is built from capillary endothelial cells sealed by tight junctions, a basement membrane, and the end-feet of astrocytes wrapped around the capillary. Together they let needed substances through while keeping out many toxins, drugs, and pathogens.
notes: Returning CSF to the blood happens at the arachnoid granulations, which drain into the superior sagittal sinus. Choose them for a question about where CSF is reabsorbed.
Correct. The blood-brain barrier controls what passes from the blood into the brain tissue.
Cushioning the brain is the job of the cerebrospinal fluid itself. It would be the answer for a question about buoyancy and shock absorption.
Producing CSF is the job of the choroid plexus, capillary networks wrapped in ependymal cells inside the ventricles. Pick it for a question about where CSF is made.
questions.answerText: It limits what passes from blood into brain tissue

questions.topic: Meninges, ventricles, CSF and brain blood supply
questions.q: Which narrow channel runs through the midbrain carrying cerebrospinal fluid?
options: The central canal
The cerebral aqueduct
The interventricular foramen
The fourth ventricle
questions.why: The cerebral aqueduct, also called the aqueduct of Sylvius, is a narrow channel through the midbrain. It carries cerebrospinal fluid from the third ventricle in the diencephalon down to the fourth ventricle behind the pons. Because it is so narrow, a blockage here is a classic cause of hydrocephalus.
